2607.13314.title: Tabular Foundation Models for Discrete Choice Estimation
2607.13314.paper_summary: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) generate predictions on structured data via in-context learning, without task-specific estimation. We ask whether TFMs can be effectively applied to discrete choice, a central demand estimation framework in marketing and operations, and find that directly applying TFMs yields limited performance. The gap is structural: TFMs assume row-independent observations, whereas discrete choice is inherently set-valued and subject to persistent consumer preference heterogeneity. We propose a reformulation that encodes both choice-set dependence and individual heterogeneity within a row-based learning framework. Evaluated on a yogurt scanner panel, individual-level heterogeneity encoding is the dominant driver of predictive accuracy. The best reformulation outperforms hierarchical Bayesian estimation by 8\% in holdout log-likelihood and 3.6\% in hit rate, running 16 times faster, a practical advantage for large-scale demand estimation. The advantage is largest in the medium-data regime (10--40 purchase occasions per consumer), where parametric Bayesian shrinkage most distorts estimates for atypical consumers. Fine-tuning on population choice data provides additional gains for consumers with shallow purchase histories, where in-context learning has limited individual-specific signal to condition on. These results establish a principled approach for applying foundation models to consumer choice problems more broadly.
2607.13314.paper_summary_zh: 表格基礎模型（TFMs）透過上下文學習在結構化數據上生成預測，而無需特定任務的估計。我們探討TFMs是否可以有效應用於離散選擇，這是一個在市場營銷和運營中中心的需求估計框架，並發現直接應用TFMs的效果有限。這一差距是結構性的：TFMs假設行獨立觀察，而離散選擇本質上是集合值的，並受到持續的消費者偏好異質性的影響。我們提出了一種重新表述，將選擇集依賴性和個體異質性編碼在基於行的學習框架中。在酸奶掃描面板上評估時，個體層級的異質性編碼是預測準確性的主要驅動因素。最佳的重新表述在保留對數似然上比層級貝葉斯估計高出8\%，在命中率上高出3.6\%，運行速度快了16倍，這對於大規模需求估計來說是一個實際優勢。在中等數據範疇（每位消費者10到40次購買機會）中，這一優勢最大，因為參數貝葉斯收縮最扭曲對於不典型消費者的估計。對於購買歷史較淺的消費者，對人口選擇數據的微調提供了額外的增益，因為在上下文學習中，個體特定的信號有限。這些結果建立了一種原則性的方法，以更廣泛地將基礎模型應用於消費者選擇問題。
